old_prompt:
Output exactly one concise, information‑dense caption: a single grammatical sentence composed of comma‑separated short phrases. Produce only that single sentence and nothing else.

Follow these deterministic, implementation‑friendly rules when forming the caption. Apply numeric verification where available, but allow pragmatic heuristics if exact detectors are unavailable. Keep all VERIFIED tokens and pronouns precise; never invent brands, celebrity names, ages, emotions, intentions, or unsupported attributes.

1) Subject groups and placement
- Identify up to 1–3 prominent subject groups in order of prominence. Front‑load subject nouns and any VERIFIED discriminative props so they appear within the first 6–8 words. Use spatial anchors (left/center/right) and include "foreground"/"background" only when depth is VERIFIED (rule 4). Use a digit only if Count is VERIFIED; otherwise use singular/plural noun forms (person/people, dog/dogs, vehicle/vehicles).

2) Count verification (relaxed)
- Emit a digit only when either (a) each instance has visible_fraction ≥ 0.45, centroid distance between instances ≥ 0.10 × image_width, and pairwise IoU < 0.10; OR (b) a clear repeating/patterned structure is detected (e.g., chorus line, row of identical performers) and instances are visually separable even if some are partially occluded. If Count is not VERIFIED, use a plural noun without a digit.

3) Contact / micro‑action verification (practical)
- Assert a contact micro‑action only when overlap_area / min(bbox_area) ≥ 0.10 AND there is contiguous boundary evidence (≈6+ adjacent overlap pixels), OR contact_classifier_confidence ≥ 0.55. If between borderline thresholds (≈0.07–0.10), use "near" phrasing (e.g., "right hand near woven basket"). When VERIFIED, include exactly one micro‑action using the template: "left|right [hand|foot|part] [strong‑verb] [object]" (e.g., "right hand holding woven basket"). Motion verbs (jumping, diving, running, holding) are allowed only with VERIFIED contact or motion evidence (airborne pose, strong motion blur, or motion_classifier_confidence ≥ 0.60).

4) Depth / foreground verification
- Include "foreground"/"background" when EITHER (a) subject_bbox_area ≥ 1.5 × any overlapping bbox_area AND pairwise IoU < 0.20 AND subject centroid is lower (visually in front), OR (b) segmentation mask shows >60% unoccluded area. Otherwise omit depth tokens.

5) Fine classes & cue‑pair pragmatics
- Emit a fine class (bicycle, motorbike/scooter, vendor/produce stand, ladder, performer, etc.) only when EITHER classifier_confidence ≥ 0.60 OR a prescribed cue‑pair is spatially satisfied within ~12% image width. Recognized cue‑pairs remain as defined (spokes+pedals ⇒ bicycle, engine casing+exhaust ⇒ motorbike, baskets+scale ⇒ vendor, rungs+rails ⇒ ladder, stage+audience or mic+facing_audience ⇒ performer). If cue‑pair fails and no classifier_confidence, use a dataset‑aware fallback from the lexicon: woven basket, pile of fruit, two‑wheeled vehicle, painted metal shutter, signboard/marquee, storefront, cart, minivan, pillow, chorus line, parade. Prefer marquee/storefront fallbacks for street/performance scenes.

6) OCR / signage (practical, high‑value)
- Quote exact text only when OCR_confidence ≥ 0.65 AND text_bbox_area ≥ 0.003 × image_area AND contrast_ratio ≥ 1.5 (or font_size_estimate ≥ 7pt). Allow a targeted exception to quote short, uppercase, centered marquee text (≤3 words) when OCR_confidence ≥ 0.60 and text_bbox_area ≥ 0.004 × image_area and local saliency/objectness is high. Otherwise do NOT invent characters; emit a compact positional descriptor (e.g., "marquee behind", "two red rectangular signs at upper right").

7) Descriptor priority and pruning (preserve discriminative tokens)
- Descriptor priority (high → low): (A) VERIFIED discriminative props or quoted text, (B) VERIFIED part‑relations/micro‑actions, (C) VERIFIED fine class, (D) clothing & clear pose/orientation, (E) color & costume patterns, (F) object state/material, (G) viewpoint/orientation, (H) lighting/reflection, (I) background. Note: color and costume descriptors are promoted above material/lighting because patterned costumes and colors are highly discriminative; text‑bearing structural backgrounds (marquee, storefront, stage) are treated as high‑priority background anchors and should be retained when VERIFIED.
- Target length: aim for 10–14 words. Hard cap: 18 words. Allow up to 20 words only when a quoted text string is emitted or two VERIFIED fine classes are present. When over cap, prune iteratively in this order: H (lighting) → F (material/texture) → I (background) unless a background is text‑bearing or structural and VERIFIED (then keep). Never drop VERIFIED tokens from categories A–C or VERIFIED part‑relations. Tie‑break removals by token length then lexicographic order.

8) Spatial relations and salient nearby objects
- Include up to 2–3 highest‑confidence nearby salient objects and their compact spatial relations (left/right/behind/among) when those objects are VERIFIED or high‑priority discriminative tokens. Prioritize inclusion of any verified signboard/marquee as a background anchor phrase (e.g., "marquee behind", "storefront behind") even if background area is modest.

9) Cropping and occlusion
- If subject_bbox_intersection_area / subject_bbox_area < 0.95, append a compact phrase "partially cropped at [top|bottom|left|right]" indicating the clipped side(s).

10) Anti‑hallucination and safe fallbacks
- Never invent brand names, celebrity names, ages, emotions, intentions, or unseen attributes. Avoid hedged language like "probably" in the final caption; prefer safe fallbacks from the lexicon when uncertain. Use plural nouns without digits when counts are not VERIFIED.

11) Implementation/diagnostics (developer only)
- Internally record which numeric checks passed (Count/Contact/Depth/OCR/FineClass) for each emitted token to aid calibration. Do NOT include these diagnostics in the caption.

Micro‑templates and exemplars (follow these patterns exactly as style examples; they obey the rules above):
- "1 woman center foreground, right hand holding woven basket of oranges, storefront behind."
- "two dogs left foreground, small white dog jumping at car passenger window, woman leaning out."
- "1 person right foreground, standing by two‑wheeled vehicle with visible pedals and chain, metal shutter behind."
- "1 boy center foreground, seated on red toy ride, playground court behind."
- "many dancers center foreground, line of red/gold sequined costumes, marquee behind."
- Borderline OCR/contact examples:
  - "1 man left foreground, three red rectangular signs at upper right, bridge behind."
  - "1 child center foreground, right hand near woven basket, wet pavement reflecting light."
  - "people center foreground, clustered near storefront, raincoats visible."

Final emission rule: apply the verification rules and pruning deterministically, assemble a single comma‑separated grammatical sentence that is concise and information‑dense, and output exactly that one caption sentence and nothing else.

- Emit a micro‑action ONLY when Contact_verified == TRUE, defined as overlap_area / min(bbox_area) ≥ 0.10 AND contiguous boundary evidence (≈6+ adjacent overlap pixels), OR contact_classifier_confidence ≥ 0.55.  
- When Contact_verified == TRUE → emit exactly one micro‑action using this template: "left|right [hand|foot|part] [strong‑verb] [object]" (example: "right hand holding woven basket"). Motion verbs are allowed only with verified contact or motion_classifier_confidence ≥ 0.60.  
- When Contact_verified == FALSE → emit the conservative fallback template: "[part] near [object]" (example: "right hand near woven basket").

4) Depth / foreground verification (hard gate)
- Include "foreground"/"background" ONLY when Depth_verified == TRUE, defined as EITHER (a) subject_bbox_area ≥ 1.5 × any overlapping bbox_area AND pairwise IoU < 0.20 AND subject centroid is lower, OR (b) segmentation mask shows >60% unoccluded area.  
- If Depth_verified == FALSE → omit depth tokens.

5) Fine class & cue‑pair verification (hard gate)
- Emit a fine class (bicycle, motorbike/scooter, vendor/produce stand, ladder, performer, etc.) ONLY when FineClass_verified == TRUE, defined as classifier_confidence ≥ 0.60 OR a prescribed cue‑pair spatially satisfied within 12% image width (e.g., spokes+pedals ⇒ bicycle, engine+exhaust ⇒ motorbike, baskets+scale ⇒ vendor, rungs+rails ⇒ ladder, stage+audience or mic+facing_audience ⇒ performer).  
- If FineClass_verified == FALSE → emit a dataset‑aware fallback token from the lexicon (storefront, painted metal shutter, two‑wheeled vehicle, woven basket, cart, marquee).

6) OCR / signage quoting (absolute policy)
- Quote exact text ONLY when OCR_quote_verified == TRUE, defined as OCR_confidence ≥ 0.65 AND text_bbox_area ≥ 0.003 × image_area AND contrast_ratio ≥ 1.5 (exception for short uppercase centered marquee ≤3 words when OCR_confidence ≥ 0.60 and text_bbox_area ≥ 0.004 × image_area).  
- If OCR_quote_verified == FALSE → NEVER quote characters; instead emit a compact positional descriptor such as "marquee behind", "storefront behind", or "three red rectangular signs at upper right" as the fallback.

7) Priority of descriptors and deterministic pruning
- Preserve VERIFIED tokens in priority order (high → low): (A) VERIFIED discriminative props or quoted text, (B) VERIFIED part‑relations/micro‑actions, (C) VERIFIED fine class, (D) clothing & clear pose/orientation, (E) color & costume patterns, (F) object state/material, (G) viewpoint/orientation, (H) lighting/reflection, (I) background.  
- Pruning algorithm (executable): if caption exceeds target/hard cap, iteratively remove tokens from categories in this exact order: H → F → I. NEVER remove VERIFIED tokens from categories A–C or any VERIFIED micro‑action. When multiple candidates equal priority, drop longest token first, then lexicographic tie‑break. Continue until within hard cap.

8) High‑value prop/anchor checklist (attempt detection in priority order)
- Always attempt to VERIFY and emit these high‑value anchors when present (thresholds above): amp/guitar case, small boats/canopies/awnings, pontoon/pavilion/shrine, corrugated metal shutter, marquee/storefront, bridge rails/diagonal rail, trash can/bin, red rectangular signs, flagpole, guitar/amp case, visible rippling reflections. If verification fails for a listed anchor → use the lexicon fallback token (e.g., "storefront behind", "marquee behind", "painted metal shutter").

9) Cropping and occlusion
- If subject_bbox_intersection_area / subject_bbox_area < 0.95 and verified as cropped → append compact phrase "partially cropped at [top|bottom|left|right]" indicating clipped side(s). Only emit when verified.

10) Anti‑hallucination rules (absolute)
- Never invent characters in text, partial quoted text, guessed words on signs, brands, ages, emotions, intentions, or unsupported attributes. Do not output probabilistic hedges ("probably", "maybe") in the final caption. If uncertain, use the prescribed lexicon fallback tokens.

11) Saliency bias
- When multiple VERIFIED tokens compete, prefer the token(s) that localize to higher visual saliency (strong edges, high contrast text, faces, large color patches). Use saliency to break ties between similarly verified candidates.

12) Micro‑template bank (preferred shapes)
- Favor captions that match these shapes exactly:  
  - "1 woman center foreground, right hand holding woven basket of oranges, storefront behind."  
  - "two dogs left foreground, small white dog jumping at car passenger window, woman leaning out."  
  - "1 person right foreground, standing by two‑wheeled vehicle with visible pedals and chain, metal shutter behind."  
  - "many dancers center foreground, line of red/gold sequined costumes, marquee behind."  
- Negative examples (forbidden hallucinations):  
  - do NOT output quoted text unless OCR_quote_verified == TRUE (e.g., do NOT output "LE MIGNON" unless verified).  
  - do NOT use vague fallbacks like "platform" when a specific verified anchor exists (use "pontoon pavilion" if verified).  
  - do NOT invent brands, celebrity names, ages, or emotions.

Final emission rule: apply the verification gates and the assembly pipeline deterministically, prune per the pruning algorithm if needed, assemble a single comma‑separated grammatical sentence that is concise and information‑dense, and output exactly that one caption sentence and nothing else.

Summary recommendations to raise CLIP image–text alignment by making the global captioning prompt stricter, more verification‑driven, and more front‑loaded with verified discriminative cues:

1) Force front‑loading of discriminative tokens
- Require the caption to begin (within first 6–8 words) with up to 1–3 subject groups plus any VERIFIED discriminative prop(s) (e.g., “person with amp”, “pontoon shrine”), using the exact micro‑template style already present.

2) Make verification gates explicit and non‑negotiable
- Embed the numeric thresholds for Count / Contact / Depth / OCR / FineClass checks in the prompt and mandate emitting tokens only when those checks pass. (Use the same practical thresholds present in your rules: visible_fraction ≥0.45, centroid distance ≥0.10×width, IoU <0.10, contact overlap_area/min_bbox ≥0.10 with contiguous boundary evidence, OCR_confidence thresholds, etc.)  
- Spell out that failure to meet a threshold requires the safe fallback lexicon (plural nouns, “storefront behind”, positional descriptors) rather than guessing.

3) Require concrete small‑prop and structural anchors
- Instruct the model to explicitly attempt to detect and emit small but discriminative foreground props and architectural anchors when visible (examples: canopies/awnings, railings/flagpoles, small boats, amps/guitar cases, corrugated metal shutter, marquee/storefront, bridge rails, trash cans). Treat these as high‑priority background/anchor phrases when VERIFIED.

4) Tighten person descriptions and micro‑actions
- Require explicit clothing/pattern color and pose/orientation and accessories when those are visually supported.  
- Enforce the single micro‑action template exactly when contact/motion evidence is VERIFIED; otherwise use conservative “near” phrasing. Disallow unverified motion/emotion words.

5) OCR/signage handling: strict quoting policy
- Keep the current OCR thresholds and require quoting exact text only when thresholds are met; otherwise require a compact positional descriptor (e.g., “marquee behind”, “three red rectangular signs at upper right”). Make this explicit in the prompt so models stop inventing short text.

6) Depth, occlusion and cropping tokens only when verified
- Keep “foreground/background” and “partially cropped at …” guarded by the existing depth/occlusion checks and require emitting them only when the numeric conditions pass.

7) Enforce descriptor priority, pruning, and hard length cap
- Embed the descriptor priority and pruning order in the prompt and require deterministic iterative pruning (H → F → I) when the caption would exceed the 10–14 word target or hard cap. Explicitly forbid dropping VERIFIED tokens from categories A–C or VERIFIED micro‑actions. Make the hard cap enforcement explicit to reduce the present overlength captions.

8) Templates and negative examples
- Add a short bank of micro‑templates (subject + verified prop + optional VERIFIED micro‑action + verified anchor) and a few negative examples showing unacceptable hallucinations (invented brands, quoted text without OCR support, generic “platform”) to train behavior.

9) Diagnostics and reproducibility
- Require the model to internally log which numeric checks passed per token (for offline calibration) but never emit diagnostics in captions.

Immediate prompt edits (concise):
- “Front‑load 1–3 subject groups + VERIFIED discriminative props within first 6–8 words; emit counts/contacts/depth/OCR/fine‑class tokens only when numeric thresholds pass; if a threshold fails use safe fallbacks from the lexicon; include one micro‑action only when contact is VERIFIED using the exact template; quote text only when OCR thresholds pass; include cropping/foreground tokens only when depth checks pass; enforce pruning (H→F→I) to meet 10–14 word target and hard cap; do not invent brands/ages/emotions.”

These changes will reduce hallucination, increase inclusion of concrete, CLIP‑salient anchors (props, signage, micro‑actions), and enforce brevity—together improving image–text similarity.

textgrad_loss_text:
Summary: current prompt is precise but too brittle — captions are losing discriminative, high‑saliency details (signage, counts, verified contact/actions, fine classes), which lowers CLIP similarity. Make the verification rules and assembly instructions more targeted, less likely to force generic fallbacks, and explicitly require anchoring details that CLIP scores highly.

Suggested prompt updates (actionable, reusable)

1. Front‑load discriminative tokens: require the caption to begin (within first 6–8 words) with verified subject(s) and any verified high‑value prop (sign, marquee, ladder, flagpole, bicycle, instrument). State this explicitly as a high priority in the prompt.

2. Force explicit signage/OCR handling: insist on quoting exact text only when OCR_confidence ≥ 0.65 and text bbox and contrast rules pass; otherwise require a compact positional descriptor (e.g., "storefront behind", "marquee above left", "three red signs upper right"). Make this a mandatory branch to avoid silent omission.

3. Make counts useful and reliable: keep the Count_verified gate but (a) require the model to compute and emit counts when geometric/segmentation evidence is present, and (b) if geometric evidence fails but a strong detection confidence exists (classifier_confidence ≥ 0.70), allow an explicit “count (verified by detector)” emission rather than forcing a generic plural. This reduces overuse of non‑informative fallbacks.

4. Tighten micro‑action/contact rules but avoid empty output: preserve the exact micro‑action template when contact is verified; if not, emit the conservative "[part] near [object]" fallback — and add a short clause instructing the model to try both contact and motion classifiers before falling back, so it will capture dynamic verbs when visually supported.

5. Require fine‑class cue verification for dataset‑relevant objects: explicitly list ladder, vendor stand, bicycle, performer, storefront etc., with the existing cue‑pair rules and classifier threshold (≥0.60). If not verified, demand the dataset lexicon fallback (storefront, painted metal shutter, two‑wheeled vehicle, woven basket, cart, marquee) — do not allow free text synonyms.

6. Spatial relations and counts as first‑class outputs: require short, comma‑separated positional phrases (left/right/center, foreground/midground/behind, near/behind/above) and explicit counts for people/objects when verified. Encourage short numeric tokens (digits) only when count gate passes.

7. Depth, cropping, and occlusion only when verified: keep these strict but require the model to attempt depth/crop verification (segmentation overlap, bbox area ratios) and emit compact phrases ("foreground", "partially cropped at bottom") only when true.

8. High‑value anchor checklist: require the model to attempt verification of the prioritized anchors (marquee/storefront, corrugated shutter, flagpole, red rectangular signs, guitar/amp case, boats/canopies). If verification fails, instruct use of the specified compact fallback token rather than inventing alternatives.

9. Pruning & length control: keep the deterministic pruning order (H→F→I) but add an explicit cap target (10–14 words) and instruct the model to compress long adjective chains into single compact descriptors (e.g., "rustic wooden facade" not multiple adjectives). Emphasize never to drop VERIFIED tokens A–C.

10. Anti‑hallucination and deterministic templates: reiterate absolute rules against inventing brands/text/people attributes; require the micro‑template bank shapes as preferred outputs and prohibit quoted text unless OCR gate passes.

11. Diagnostics and fallback softening: to improve CLIP alignment, add a single soft fallback allowance: if the model has medium confidence (0.50–0.70) for a high‑saliency anchor (text, large sign, distinctive prop) but geometric gates fail, allow emitting a compact low‑risk descriptor (e.g., "sign behind" vs. generic "storefront") flagged as low‑certainty — this reduces generic fallbacks while preserving anti‑hallucination.

12. Evaluation feedback loop: add an instruction that captions should prioritize content that CLIP correlates with—salient text, unique props, clear actions, and counts—and explicitly prefer those tokens when multiple VERIFIED options exist (saliency tie‑break).

Implementation note: codify verification checks (OCR, contact, count, fine class, depth) as explicit substeps in the prompt so the model executes them in order and substitutes the exact lexicon fallback when gates fail. This keeps outputs deterministic, reduces hallucination, and boosts inclusion of the discriminative elements that raise CLIP similarity.

textgrad_loss_text:
Summary recommendations to improve CLIP alignment (concise, actionable prompt changes)

- Promote scene-level anchors and dynamic context: require the prompt to prioritize explicit environment tokens (water/river/ghats/temple/boats, marquee/storefront, embankment/trees) whenever visual evidence or saliency supports them, so captions include background architecture and setting rather than only foreground people/objects.

- Make micro‑action rules less brittle: allow MEDIUM‑band emission of motion verbs when motion_confidence + geometry indicate movement (e.g., "jumping", "clearing", "pawing") and expand the MEDIUM micro‑verb whitelist to include dynamic verbs observed in critiques (jumping, pawing, showing, speaking, jumping/clearing).

- Strengthen spatial relations and group/formation descriptions: instruct captioner to emit explicit spatial tokens (center/left/right, foreground/background, alongside/moored beside, flanking) and group formation phrases (chorus line, seated group watching) when geometric or segmentation cues exist.

- Expand MEDIUM fine‑class whitelist and anchor vocabulary: add high‑utility scene labels (boat, shrine/temple, steps/ghats, parade performer, children) and anchors (boats/canopies, flagpoles, hedgerow/trees) so useful mid‑confidence detections are expressible without falling back to vague dataset lexicon.

- Reduce hallucination by tightening fallbacks and prohibiting invented props: when an object is LOW evidence, force neutral fallback tokens (e.g., "object on table", "storefront behind") and explicitly forbid substituting plausible but unverified specific objects (no invented baskets, brand names, or actions).

- Make first‑words constraint robust to detector timing: change the “first 6–8 words must contain subject + HIGH anchor” rule to allow a MEDIUM anchor subject pairing (subject or plural fallback + MEDIUM anchor) so captions do not default to generic plural fallbacks merely because an anchor is verified slightly later.

- Preserve essential tokens during pruning: change the pruning priority to never remove the micro‑action or the fine‑class slot (slots 1–3) even under length pressure; if something must be pruned, remove less informative background descriptors first.

- Require descriptive clothing/appearance only when verifiable: emit clothing/pose tokens only at MEDIUM/HIGH to avoid spurious color/pattern claims; when MEDIUM, restrict to short allowed phrases (e.g., "red/white stripes") rather than free adjectives.

- Improve OCR/signage handling for CLIP: allow MEDIUM OCR descriptors to include short readable words/letters if OCR_confidence supports partial reads (but still forbid brand invention), and prioritize marquee/text tokens when salient so CLIP can match visible text.

- Encourage mention of reflections, motion cues and relative sizes: instruct the model to include visible cues that CLIP keys on (reflections on water, airborne pose, paws off ground, larger vs. smaller dog) when corresponding motion/saliency evidence is present.

Implementing these changes will reduce fallback-induced generic captions, increase inclusion of high‑value scene anchors and dynamic cues, and better align generated captions with CLIP’s visual-text sensitivity.

old_prompt:
Output exactly one concise, information‑dense caption: a single grammatical sentence composed of comma‑separated short phrases. Produce only that one sentence and nothing else.

Assembly order (emit in this order; append only one token per slot unless slot allows multiple):
1) Subject group(s) and high‑value anchor/prop (0–3 groups; must appear first).
2) Micro‑action / contact (use exact micro‑templates below).
3) Fine class (verified label or dataset lexicon fallback).
4) Clothing / clear pose / orientation (emit only when MEDIUM/HIGH verified).
5) Up to two anchors/signage (only if verified; otherwise use neutral positional fallback tokens).
6) Spatial/cropping/depth token (only if verified).

Verification bands and safe emission
- Use detectors/geometry/segmentation/motion/OCR/saliency to map evidence to HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW.
- HIGH: emit the verified token exactly from the detector.
- MEDIUM: emit only tokens from the curated MEDIUM whitelists below.
- LOW: emit conservative, neutral fallback tokens (examples: "storefront behind", "boats moored beside", "object on table", "painted metal shutter").

Micro‑action / contact template rules
- HIGH: exact template "left|right [hand|foot|part] [strong‑verb] [object]" (e.g., "right hand holding basket").
- MEDIUM: allow a constrained dynamic verb whitelist when supported by complementary evidence (motion_confidence or segmentation + saliency). MEDIUM verb whitelist (examples): jumping, pawing, clearing, showing, speaking, holding, carrying, pushing, pulling.
- LOW: conservative fallback "[part] near [object]" (e.g., "right hand near object").
- Never use hedges or speculative wording; always use the strict template form.

First‑words requirement (robust)
- The first 6–8 words must contain the subject group token (or a plural fallback noun) and either a HIGH anchor OR a MEDIUM anchor from the MEDIUM anchor whitelist. If no such anchor appears by the 8th word, emit the plural fallback subject token first and include anchors later as positional fallbacks.

Count and numeric rules
- Emit digits only when count is HIGH verified by geometry/segmentation or detector_count_confidence ≥ 0.70. Otherwise use plural fallback nouns (people/dogs/vehicles/group of people). Do not append qualifiers.

Fine‑class, anchors, and MEDIUM whitelists (use MEDIUM items only when evidence is MEDIUM)
- Expand MEDIUM fine‑class whitelist to include: boat, canoe, shrine/temple, ghats/steps, children/children group, performer/chorus line, vendor/produce stand, parade participant.
- Expand MEDIUM anchor whitelist to include: marquee, boats/canopies, flagpole, ladder, bicycle/two‑wheeled vehicle, hedgerow/trees.
- If LOW, use neutral fallbacks; never invent specific unverified props.

Spatial relations and formation tokens
- When geometry/segmentation is reliable, emit explicit spatial tokens (left/right/center/foreground/background, alongside/moored beside, flanking, seated group watching). Make spatial phrases MEDIUM‑eligible from a short whitelist.

OCR / signage handling
- HIGH OCR: quote exact text (counts toward length).
- MEDIUM OCR: allow low‑risk signage descriptors and short high‑confidence partial reads (single words or up to 6 visible letters) only when OCR_confidence ≥ MEDIUM and saliency is high; do not invent or complete partial brand names.
- LOW: emit positional signage fallbacks (e.g., "marquee above", "large red sign upper right").

Saliency tie‑breaking and selection
- When multiple VERIFIED candidates compete, prefer by saliency: text > large object/prop > face > large color patch/clothing. Bias toward anchors that are highly salient even if detector confidence is MEDIUM.

Pruning, compression, and length control
- Target length: 10–16 words. Hard cap: 20 words. Allow up to +2 words beyond target only when including both a HIGH‑verified fine class and a HIGH‑verified anchor.
- Pruning priority (apply deterministically when over cap):
   1) Compress adjective chains into compact noun phrases.
   2) Remove lighting/reflection descriptors first.
   3) Remove object state/material next.
   4) Remove background/ancillary context last.
- Never remove tokens from slots 1–3 (subject, micro‑action, fine class). Preserve MEDIUM tokens in slots 1–3 when present.
- Continue pruning until within cap. If still over cap, construct a minimal safe caption that uses available HIGH or MEDIUM tokens (prefer MEDIUM anchors/fine classes over generic fallbacks).

De‑duplication and normalization
- Collapse exact repeated phrases and repeated tokens. Merge adjective chains (e.g., "rustic wooden facade"). Prohibit repeating the same phrase.

Anti‑hallucination absolutes
- Never invent brand names, partial/completed text, ages, emotions, intentions, or unsupported attributes. Do not add hedges. When verification is insufficient, use the prescribed neutral fallbacks. If a MID‑confidence token is available, prefer enumerated MEDIUM whitelist tokens rather than free adjectives.

Final validator (must pass)
- One grammatical sentence of comma‑separated short phrases.
- Length within caps.
- First 6–8 words include subject or plural fallback plus a HIGH or MEDIUM anchor.
- No hedges, no invented brands/text, no duplicated phrases.
- Only allowed MEDIUM tokens are emitted under MEDIUM band.
- If validator would fail, emit a minimal safe caption constructed from available HIGH or MEDIUM tokens (subject plural fallback if necessary), using neutral positional fallbacks and preserving any MEDIUM fine class or anchor evidence.

Preferred micro‑templates (use when slots permit; adapt to verification):
- "1 woman center foreground, right hand holding basket, shrine behind."
- "group of performers center left, chorus line stretching across crosswalk, marquee above."
- "two dogs left foreground, small white dog mid‑air at passenger window, woman leaning out."

Produce only the single validated sentence as the final caption.

Final validator (must pass before emitting):

- Length within caps and target rules.
- First 6–8 words include subject token (or plural fallback) plus a HIGH or MEDIUM anchor (or neutral anchor fallback if no MEDIUM/HIGH).
- Micro‑action slot present and follows template rules.
- No hedges, no invented brands/text, no duplicated phrases.
- Only allowed MEDIUM tokens are emitted under MEDIUM band.
- If validator would fail, emit the deterministic minimal safe caption described above.

Short positive example (ideal):
- "group of people, right hand holding red shopping bag, storefront behind, marquee above."

Short negative example (avoid):
- "Several people maybe near a building with an unclear sign and someone possibly holding something."

Machine‑readable checklist to append internally (for validation):
- OCR → include if HIGH/MEDIUM; quote only if HIGH (MEDIUM only one short token ≤6 chars).
- Micro‑action → always emit (HIGH template or MEDIUM whitelist or LOW fallback).
- Anchor/text → must appear within first 8 words if MEDIUM/HIGH, else include neutral anchor fallback early.
- Counts → digits only if detector_count_confidence ≥ 0.70.

textgrad_loss_text:
Summary diagnosis: captions are too generic and omit high‑value anchors, legible text, precise micro‑actions, counts/localization and distinctive object/material cues that drive CLIP similarity; pruning/length rules sometimes remove the most valuable tokens.

Concrete, reusable prompt changes (apply globally)

1. Anchor & OCR prioritization
- Instruct the model to always attempt OCR on salient signage and to include exact quoted text only for HIGH OCR evidence; for MEDIUM OCR allow short single‑word/6‑letter reads. Place any quoted or MEDIUM anchor token in the early token slots (within the first 6–8 words) to maximize CLIP alignment.
- Explicitly prioritize high‑saliency anchors over background adjectives: text > large object/prop > face > clothing patch.

2. Micro‑action templates and verification
- Require the strict micro‑action template when motion/contact evidence is MEDIUM/HIGH: HIGH = exact "left|right [hand|foot|part] [strong‑verb] [object]"; MEDIUM = constrained verb whitelist (jumping, holding, carrying, showing, speaking, pushing, pulling); LOW = fallback "[part] near [object]".
- Make micro‑action slot mandatory and non‑prunable; when micro‑action verification is LOW, emit the safe fallback form rather than omitting it.

3. Counts, localization, and posture
- Require explicit person/subject counts and 1–2 spatial localization tokens when detector_count_confidence ≥ 0.70 or segmentation reliably separates subjects. Otherwise emit plural fallbacks (people/children/vehicles).
- Mandate short posture/orientation tokens (center/left/right, foreground/background, seated/standing/leaning) whenever geometry/pose detectors give MEDIUM/HIGH evidence.

4. Fine classes and specific objects
- Instruct the model to prefer dataset-lexicon fine classes or concrete object types (e.g., acoustic guitar, leaf pile, vendor stand) when any detector yields MEDIUM/HIGH evidence. Treat these tokens as protected slots (not to be pruned before slots 1–3).

5. Material/architectural/prop detail
- Encourage inclusion of distinctive, verifiable material/architectural descriptors (e.g., "rustic wooden facade," "metal/rusted roof," "wooden posts," "mounted fish display") only when segmentation/saliency supports MEDIUM/HIGH; otherwise use neutral fallbacks like "storefront behind" or "marquee above."

6. Saliency‑driven selection & ordering
- Add explicit saliency tie‑breaking rules to the prompt: when multiple candidates exist, pick the most salient anchor (text > large prop > face). Require that the chosen anchor appears early (first 6–8 words) and that subject + anchor co‑occur in the initial phrase.

7. Pruning and length policy refinement
- Keep current pruning priorities but forbid removal of slots 1–3. When pruning is required, explicitly remove lighting/reflection descriptors first, then material/state, then background. Cap target length to 10–16 words and enforce the +2 exception only when BOTH a HIGH fine class and a HIGH anchor are present.

8. MEDIUM whitelist expansions & strictness
- Expand and codify the MEDIUM whitelists to cover likely dataset items observed in failures (vendor/produce stand, marquee, flagpole, hedgerow/trees, bicycle). Allow MEDIUM clothing tokens (e.g., "navy sweater") only when color/texture detectors reach MEDIUM confidence.

9. Anti‑hallucination tightening
- Reiterate absolute bans: no invented brands/text/ages/emotions/intentions. Require neutral positional fallbacks when verification is LOW (e.g., "marquee above", "storefront behind", "object on table").

10. Prompt wording & examples
- Provide compact positive and negative examples in the prompt: show one ideal caption that includes subject + HIGH/MEDIUM anchor early + strict micro‑action + fine class + a verified clothing/pose token; show one bad caption that omits text/anchor or uses hedging. This steers model behavior toward CLIP‑friendly concreteness.

Checklist to include in the global prompt footer (machine‑readable)
- OCR → include if HIGH/MEDIUM; quote only if HIGH.
- Micro‑action → always emit (HIGH/MEDIUM template or LOW fallback).
- Anchor/text → must appear within first 8 words if MEDIUM/HIGH.
- Counts → digits only if detector_count_confidence ≥ 0.70 else use plural fallback.
- Prune per priority; never prune slots 1–3.
- If verification insufficient → use neutral fallbacks.

Rationale summary: forcing early, verifiable anchors/text, precise micro‑actions, and compact spatial/person tokens increases overlap with CLIP’s high‑value visual-word activations; stricter anti‑hallucination fallbacks prevent spurious details that lower similarity. Implementing these template and verification refinements should raise mean CLIP similarity while preserving SigLIP behavior.

3) Fine class (verified label or dataset lexicon token; if no verified fine class, use a safe plural fallback such as "people/dogs/vehicles/vendor stand").
4) Clothing / clear pose / orientation — include only when MEDIUM/HIGH verified.
5) Up to two anchors/signage (only if MEDIUM/HIGH verified; otherwise use neutral positional fallback tokens such as "marquee above", "storefront behind").
6) Spatial/cropping/depth token if verified.

Verification bands and numeric thresholds (use detector outputs where available):
- HIGH: OCR_confidence ≥ 0.85 OR segmentation_iou ≥ 0.75 OR motion_confidence ≥ 0.85.
- MEDIUM: OCR_confidence ≥ 0.50 OR segmentation_iou ≥ 0.40 OR motion_confidence ≥ 0.60 OR detector_count_confidence ≥ 0.70.
- LOW: otherwise.
- Digit counts: emit digits only if detector_count_confidence ≥ 0.70; otherwise use plural fallback nouns.

OCR and signage rules:
- If OCR is HIGH: emit exact quoted text (quote counts toward length).
- If OCR is MEDIUM and saliency is high: emit at most one short quoted token (single word or ≤6 characters); do not invent or complete partial names.
- If OCR is LOW: use a neutral positional anchor fallback (e.g., "marquee above", "large sign upper right").

First‑words requirement:
- The first 6–8 words must contain the subject group token (or a plural fallback noun) and a HIGH anchor OR a MEDIUM anchor from the MEDIUM anchor whitelist. If this fails, the caption must be auto‑rewritten into the minimal safe form: plural subject fallback + neutral anchor fallback + micro‑action LOW fallback + fine‑class fallback, all within the first 8 words.

Saliency tie‑breaking and selection:
- When multiple candidates are present, prefer in order: 1) OCR text, 2) large prop/signage, 3) face/people, 4) large color patch/clothing. Chosen anchor must appear early (within first 6–8 words).

MEDIUM whitelist (emit these exact tokens only under MEDIUM):
- Fine classes: boat, canoe, shrine/temple, ghats/steps, children, performer, vendor, vendor stand, parade participant.
- Anchors: marquee, boats, canopies, flagpole, ladder, bicycle, hedgerow, trees.
- Clothing tokens allowed under MEDIUM: "navy sweater", "red patterned dress", "white blouse".

Pruning, compression, and length control:
- Target length: 10–16 words. Hard cap: 20 words. Allow +2 words beyond target when EITHER a HIGH anchor OR a HIGH fine class is present.
- Pruning priority (apply deterministically until within cap):
   1) Compress adjective chains into compact noun phrases.
   2) Remove lighting/reflection descriptors first.
   3) Remove object state/material next.
   4) Remove background/ancillary context last.
- NEVER remove or prune tokens from slots 1–3. Preserve MEDIUM tokens in slots 1–3 when present. If still over cap, construct a minimal safe caption that preserves any HIGH/MEDIUM tokens in slots 1–3 and uses neutral fallbacks elsewhere.

Anti‑hallucination absolutes:
- Do not invent brand names, partial/complete text, ages, emotions, intentions, or unsupported attributes.
- No hedges, qualifiers, or speculative language.
- When verification is LOW, use prescribed neutral fallbacks (e.g., "storefront behind", "marquee above", "object on table", "group of people").

Final validator (must pass before emitting):
- One grammatical sentence of comma‑separated short phrases.
- Length within caps and target rules.
- First 6–8 words include subject token (or plural fallback) plus a HIGH or MEDIUM anchor (or neutral anchor fallback if no MEDIUM/HIGH).
- Micro‑action slot present and follows template rules.
- No hedges, no invented brands/text, no duplicated phrases.
- Only allowed MEDIUM tokens are emitted under MEDIUM band.
- If validator would fail, emit the deterministic minimal safe caption described above.

Short positive example (ideal):
- "group of people, right hand holding red shopping bag, storefront behind, marquee above."

Short negative example (avoid):
- "Several people maybe near a building with an unclear sign and someone possibly holding something."

Machine‑readable checklist to append internally (for validation):
- OCR → include if HIGH/MEDIUM; quote only if HIGH (MEDIUM only one short token ≤6 chars).
- Micro‑action → always emit (HIGH template or MEDIUM whitelist or LOW fallback).
- Anchor/text → must appear within first 8 words if MEDIUM/HIGH, else include neutral anchor fallback early.
- Counts → digits only if detector_count_confidence ≥ 0.70.
- Prune per priority; never prune slots 1–3.
- If validation fails → auto‑rewrite to minimal safe caption template.

Adhere strictly to these rules when generating the single final caption.
new_prompt:
Produce exactly one concise, information‑dense caption: a single grammatical sentence of comma‑separated short phrases. Output only that one sentence and nothing else.

Output slots (emit in this order; slots 1–3 are mandatory and must be preserved if they contain MEDIUM/HIGH verified tokens):
1) Subject token (0–3 subject groups) plus one chosen anchor/prop token (see deterministic anchor priority below).
2) Micro‑action / contact (always emit one, see Micro‑action rules).
3) Fine class (verified label or dataset token); if not MEDIUM/HIGH verified, use the safe plural fallback "people/dogs/vehicles/vendor stand".
4) Clothing / clear pose / orientation — include only when MEDIUM/HIGH verified.
5) Up to two anchors/signage (only if MEDIUM/HIGH verified; otherwise use neutral positional anchors such as "storefront behind", "marquee above").
6) Spatial/cropping/depth token if MEDIUM/HIGH verified.

Deterministic anchor priority (select the highest available and place it early):
- 1st: OCR text (use full quoted text if OCR_conf ≥ 0.85; else one short quoted token ≤6 chars only if 0.50 ≤ OCR_conf < 0.85 AND saliency_score ≥ threshold).
- 2nd: large prop/signage (largest segmented area or flagged prop).
- 3rd: people/faces (detected fine class).
- 4th: distinctive color/clothing patch.
Place the chosen anchor within the first 6–8 words together with the subject token. If no MEDIUM/HIGH anchor exists, use a neutral anchor and still place it within the first 8 words.

Verification gating (use provided detector/OCR/motion outputs with these actionable if/elif rules):
- OCR_HIGH: OCR_conf ≥ 0.85 → emit full quoted text and placement phrase (e.g., "on wall left").
- OCR_MED: 0.50 ≤ OCR_conf < 0.85 AND saliency_score ≥ threshold → emit one short quoted token (≤6 chars) and placement.
- Otherwise → do not emit text; use neutral positional anchor.
- SEGMENTATION_HIGH: segmentation_iou ≥ 0.75 (treat as HIGH verification).
- SEGMENTATION_MED: 0.40 ≤ segmentation_iou < 0.75 (treat as MEDIUM verification).
- COUNT_DIGITS: emit digits only if detector_count_confidence ≥ 0.70; otherwise use plural nouns. If detector strongly indicates zero, you may emit "none".

Micro‑action rules (always emit one; pick the highest evidence template available):
- HIGH evidence (use when part segmentation or motion_confidence ≥ 0.85): exact form "left|right [hand|foot|part] [strong‑verb] [object]" (e.g., "right hand holding basket").
- MEDIUM evidence (use when segmentation_iou ≥ 0.40 OR detector_confidence ≥ 0.70): pick one verb from whitelist {jumping, pawing, clearing, showing, speaking, holding, carrying, pushing, pulling, strumming, leaning}. You may append a short orientation token ("back view", "seen from behind") when MEDIUM verifies orientation.
- LOW evidence (fallback): "[part] near [object]" (e.g., "right hand near object").
Never omit or hedge this slot.

Fine class and clothing:
- Emit fine class or clothing only when verified at MEDIUM/HIGH. If not verified, use the safe plural fallback. MEDIUM whitelist tokens (boat, canoe, shrine/temple, ghats/steps, children, performer, vendor, vendor stand, parade participant, marquee, boats, canopies, flagpole, ladder, bicycle, hedgerow, trees, "navy sweater", "red patterned dress", "white blouse") may be emitted only when MEDIUM verification applies and only in their designated slot.

OCR and signage specifics:
- If emitting OCR text, always include a short placement phrase (e.g., "on wall left", "above the doorway"). Do not invent, complete, or guess partial text. If OCR_MED has low saliency, revert to a neutral anchor.

First‑words rule and deterministic minimal rewrite:
- Within the first 8 words, include the subject token (or plural fallback) and the chosen anchor token (OCR token if selected, otherwise prop/people/color anchor). If this cannot be satisfied, auto‑rewrite to this minimal safe caption exactly (use this template and nothing else):
  "group of people, storefront behind, right hand near object, people/dogs/vehicles/vendor stand."
(This minimal template is the deterministic fallback to ensure a valid single sentence when requirements fail.)

Pruning and length control:
- Target: 10–16 words. Hard cap: 22 words. Allow +2 words beyond target when a HIGH anchor is present or when BOTH a MEDIUM anchor and a MEDIUM micro‑action are present.
- Prune deterministically in this order until within caps:
  1) Compress adjective chains (e.g., "large red metal" → "large red metal" compacted).
  2) Remove lighting/reflection descriptors.
  3) Remove object state/material descriptors.
  4) Remove background/ancillary context.
- Never prune tokens used to satisfy verification rules (OCR quoted text, MEDIUM/HIGH anchors, verified counts) in slots 1–3.

Counts and numerals:
- Emit exact digits only when detector_count_confidence ≥ 0.70. Otherwise use plural nouns; do not use vague quantifiers like "several" or "a few". If detector indicates zero with high confidence, emit "none".

Anti‑hallucination absolutes (do not do these):
- Do not invent brand names, complete partial text, invent ages, emotions, intentions, or unsupported attributes.
- No hedging language or speculative words (may, maybe, possibly, appears to be).
- If a detail is not verified at MEDIUM/HIGH, replace it with an approved neutral fallback (e.g., "storefront behind", "marquee above", "object on table", "group of people").

Final validator (must pass before emitting caption):
- One grammatical sentence of comma‑separated short phrases.
- First 6–8 words include subject token (or plural fallback) and chosen anchor (or neutral anchor).
- Micro‑action slot present and follows the templates above.
- Length within caps and pruning rules applied.
- No hedges, no invented text/brands, no duplicated phrases.
- Only allowed MEDIUM tokens are used under MEDIUM verification.
- If any check fails, emit the deterministic minimal safe caption given above.

Succinct exemplars (ideal outputs for reference):
- OCR_HIGH example: "group of people, right hand holding 'Le Mignon' sign on wall left, storefront behind."
- PROP_MED example: "woman, right hand holding red shopping bag, storefront behind, marquee above."
- PEOPLE_MED example: "two people, back view sitting on bench, black tufted bench foreground, floor reflections."
- LOW evidence example: "group of people, right hand near object, people/dogs/vehicles/vendor stand."

Adhere strictly to these rules and emit only the single final caption sentence.

textgrad_loss_text:
Summary: the prompt should push the model to place one high‑saliency anchor or transcribed text early, prefer verified concrete details (counts, pose, dominant object, color/clothing) over vague/generic tokens, and enforce strict anti‑hallucination rules tied to detector/OCR/segmentation confidence.

Actionable changes (priority order)

1) Force anchor selection and early placement
- Mandate the chosen anchor (OCR text when available, else large prop/signage, else people, else clothing color) appear within the first 6–8 words. Make this deterministic in the prompt and call out the priority order.

2) Make OCR/signage rules explicit and usable
- Require inclusion of LEGIBLE text when OCR_confidence ≥ MEDIUM: one short quoted token (≤6 chars) if MEDIUM; full quoted text if HIGH. Always add its placement (e.g., "on wall left") when OCR included. Do not invent or complete partial text.

3) Tighten hallucination rules with detector thresholds
- Only mention people/animals/vehicles/vendor stands or numeric counts when detector_count_confidence ≥ 0.70 (emit digits) or segmentation_iou ≥ MEDIUM. Otherwise use the prescribed neutral fallbacks (e.g., "storefront behind", "marquee above", "group of people") or explicitly state "none" for zero when detector strongly indicates absence.

4) Require dominant object + spatial framing
- Instruct captions to identify one dominant central object/structure (storefront/bench/table) when segmentation/detection supports it, name its material/appearance only if MEDIUM/HIGH verified, and place people/actions relative to it (foreground/midground/background).

5) Micro‑action and pose rules tied to verification
- Keep the mandatory micro‑action slot but require it to reflect the highest verification band available (HIGH template when segmentation/OCR/motion passes HIGH; MEDIUM whitelist verbs only when MEDIUM verified). Add explicit allowance for geometric/orientation tokens like "back view"/"seen from behind" under MEDIUM verification.

6) Make clothing and fine class inclusion conditional
- Only emit clothing descriptors or dataset fine classes if segmentation_iou or detector confidence ≥ MEDIUM; otherwise omit these slots (use neutral fallbacks). Keep the MEDIUM whitelist but expand prompt examples to show correct placement and preservation.

7) Signage placement and multiplicity
- When signage/text is present, require: transcription (per OCR rules), placement (e.g., "above", "on wall left"), and count of identical signs when detector_count_confidence supports digits. This increases discriminative specificity for CLIP.

8) Explicit anti‑hallucination protocol
- Add a short deterministic rule block: if any element cannot be verified at MEDIUM/HIGH, replace it with an approved neutral fallback. Ban soft language; ban invented brands/partial text/ages/emotions. Make the fallback template explicit and enforceable.

9) Preserve discriminative tokens during pruning
- Update pruning priorities to never prune anchors, OCR tokens, or verified counts in slots 1–3. When over-length, compress adjectives but keep unique, CLIP‑salient tokens (text, anchor, exact color/clothing tokens).

10) Validation and auto‑rewrite policy refinement
- When the first‑words requirement would fail, auto‑rewrite to a minimal safe caption that preserves any available MEDIUM/HIGH anchor or OCR token rather than defaulting to generic fallbacks. Log which detections caused rewrite for debugging.

11) Provide succinct exemplar pairs for training/prompting
- Add 6–8 annotated positive/negative examples demonstrating: early OCR anchor inclusion, correct signage placement, exact count emission when detector confident, correct fallback when low confidence, and avoidance of speculative items.

Rationale (one line)
- These changes force captions to surface high‑saliency, image‑unique cues early (text, props, counts, dominant object, verified clothing/pose) and eliminate low‑confidence speculation—both actions that empirically raise CLIP image/text alignment.
